reference.method: SOURCE VERIFIED plus RUNTIME VERIFIED with isolated Next.js development boots using fresh temporary SQLite state

scope: HEAD, OPTIONS, unsupported methods, trailing slash, case, query preservation, and the neighboring JSON-404 boundary
ordering of normalization, proxy classification, authentication, and method handling

pipelineCors.standardAllowMethods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
pipelineCors.standardAllowHeaders: Content-Type, Authorization, x-api-key, anthropic-version, x-omniroute-connection, X-OmniRoute-Lease-Owner, X-OmniRoute-Lease-Generation, x-internal-test, accept

alias.pipelineHeaderCaveat: The authz pipeline removes or replaces trusted internal headers for both paths; this is common pipeline processing, not an alias difference.
alias.proxyAndAuthClassification: The proxy sees the public pathname before route dispatch. /models is matched by src/proxy.ts and normalized by src/server/authz/classify.ts to CLIENT_API with effective path /api/v1/models, just as /v1/models is.
alias.handlerIdentity: Both exact paths dispatch to src/app/api/v1/models/route.ts after the internal rewrite.
alias.observableDifferences: No path-specific difference was observed in status, body, route-class, CORS, or catalog headers when the exact rewrite fires. Request IDs and timing naturally differ per request.
alias.evidence: SOURCE VERIFIED; RUNTIME VERIFIED for GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, representative unsupported methods, and auth-required requests

openRuntime.cors: The pipeline supplies the global Allow-Methods and Allow-Headers values. A credentialless request with an unlisted Origin has no Access-Control-Allow-Origin; token-bearing requests use the relaxed token-auth origin rule.

execution.apiKeyLastUsed: A valid database-backed API key can update last_used_at when clientApiPolicy validates it and the update is not suppressed by the validation/update TTL. Anonymous requests and configured environment keys do not create that database-row update. This possible auth-policy side effect is separate from the explicit HEAD handler.
execution.transport: scripts/dev/head-response-guard.cjs suppresses any response bytes and adds Connection: close for every inbound HEAD before Next handles it.

head.evidence: SOURCE VERIFIED; TEST VERIFIED by tests/unit/head-request-v1-models-6400.test.ts; RUNTIME VERIFIED in open and REQUIRE_API_KEY=true isolated boots

runtime.pipelineShortCircuit: src/server/authz/pipeline.ts:359-365 returns the preflight response before policy evaluation or route dispatch

cors.accessControlAllowMethods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
cors.accessControlAllowHeaders: The raw Access-Control-Request-Headers value when supplied; otherwise pipelineCors.standardAllowHeaders
cors.accessControlAllowOrigin: The supplied Origin is echoed for a preflight on the relaxed CLIENT_API surface
cors.vary: Origin; no Accept-Encoding value is added to the 204 response

options.routeExportContrast: The explicit route export in src/app/api/v1/models/route.ts:8-15 is not reached through these public paths because the proxy short-circuits OPTIONS. Its direct Response has the route-local GET, HEAD, OPTIONS methods and wildcard headers, but the observed HTTP contract is the pipeline 204 above.
options.evidence: SOURCE VERIFIED; RUNTIME VERIFIED with representative Origin, Access-Control-Request-Method, and Access-Control-Request-Headers; TEST VERIFIED by the OPTIONS assertions in tests/unit/authz/pipeline.test.ts and the direct route test

openRuntime.handling: Next.js App Router default for a route exporting only GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS; the response is empty in the isolated development runtime
openRuntime.cors: The request has CLIENT_API pipeline route/request headers and the standard CORS method/header headers

authRequiredWithoutCredential.handling: clientApiPolicy rejects before Next.js performs route method handling

normalRouteMethods.evidence: SOURCE VERIFIED; RUNTIME VERIFIED for representative POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE requests in open mode and POST in REQUIRE_API_KEY=true mode

transportGuard.source: scripts/dev/http-method-guard.cjs and scripts/dev/run-next.mjs invoke this guard before Next/proxy processing
transportGuard.evidence: SOURCE VERIFIED; RUNTIME VERIFIED for TRACE against both exact paths

trailingSlash.configuration: next.config.mjs does not set trailingSlash; the observed Next.js default is trailingSlash=false

commonResponse.cors: No pipeline CORS headers on the raw redirect
commonResponse.head: HEAD receives the same 308 and Location/Refresh headers but zero client body bytes and Connection: close from the transport guard
commonResponse.options: OPTIONS receives the same 308 and small plain-text redirect body, without the pipeline preflight headers

trailingSlash.ordering: Next trailing-slash normalization occurs before the observed proxy/auth stage and before the alias/canonical rewrite. A separately followed request to the slashless Location is a new request and is not part of the raw redirect result.
trailingSlash.evidence: SOURCE VERIFIED for configuration; RUNTIME VERIFIED for GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS with REQUIRE_API_KEY=true, including query-bearing Locations

caseSensitivity.scope: The Models paths only; runtime observations are Linux
caseSensitivity.sourceExplanation: The proxy matcher explicitly accepts case variants of v1 and models, and Next rewrite matching is case-insensitive. src/server/authz/classify.ts recognizes the control segment case-insensitively but preserves the original-case tail. On the Linux reference runtime, /v1/Models therefore dispatches to a case-sensitive unmatched route rather than to /api/v1/models.
caseSensitivity.crossPlatform: The result of filesystem route resolution for a mixed-case tail on a case-insensitive filesystem is UNRESOLVED and must not be generalized from the Linux runtime.

queryPreservation.runtimeObservation: Both requests returned 200 with the same observable page result, body length, and X-Model-Catalog-Version value; the query was chosen so limit=1 remained observable.
queryPreservation.mechanism: The /models rewrite changes the pathname only and forwards the query string; the /v1 rewrite likewise forwards the query string to /api/v1/models.
queryPreservation.evidence: SOURCE VERIFIED; RUNTIME VERIFIED; pagination semantics remain covered by Task 003 and are not re-specified here

json404Boundary.purpose: Provide only the neighboring distinctions needed by a native Models router

probes.source: src/app/api/v1/models/[...model]/route.ts -> modelById.ts; this is a dynamic model lookup, not the v1 catch-all

probes.bodyShape: HTML not-found page; no JSON error envelope
probes.relevantHeaders: Next page-rendering headers, including Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate; no authz CORS overlay
probes.source: The alias rewrite and proxy matcher are exact /models entries; unmatched root paths fall through to the app not-found page

json404Boundary.jsonErrorHeaders: The two /v1 JSON responses carry CLIENT_API route/request headers and the standard pipeline CORS method/header headers; neither carries X-Model-Catalog-Version.
json404Boundary.authOrdering: With REQUIRE_API_KEY=true and no credential, both /v1 probes return the pipeline 401 before their respective 404 handlers. The root-level probe remains an HTML 404 because it is not covered by the Models proxy matcher.
json404Boundary.evidence: SOURCE VERIFIED; TEST VERIFIED by tests/unit/api/v1-catchall-json-404.test.ts and related catch-all tests; RUNTIME VERIFIED for all three representative paths

matchedModelsPath: Next normalizes a trailing slash first when present
proxy/classifier sees the public /v1/models or /models pathname and assigns CLIENT_API
for non-GET/non-OPTIONS methods the API body-size gate runs before policy; empty probes pass it
other methods enter clientApiPolicy; a required credential failure returns 401 before route/method handling
an allowed request reaches the internal rewrite and the same Models route handler
authOrdering.invalidMethod: A normal unsupported method therefore encounters auth before the framework 405 when authentication is required. TRACE is different: the Node transport guard returns 405 before proxy/auth.
authOrdering.trailingSlash: The raw 308 occurs before proxy/auth, including with REQUIRE_API_KEY=true.
authOrdering.aliasClassification: No canonical-vs-alias auth-order difference was observed or found in source.
authOrdering.evidence: SOURCE VERIFIED; RUNTIME VERIFIED with open and REQUIRE_API_KEY=true isolated boots

source: src/proxy.ts:23-52 (proxy matcher and Models case matching)
src/server/authz/pipeline.ts:263-446 (body-size gate, OPTIONS short circuit, policy ordering, CORS)
evidence.runtime: RUNTIME VERIFIED against an isolated Next.js development server on Linux, with fresh temporary SQLite state, both REQUIRE_API_KEY=false and REQUIRE_API_KEY=true, raw redirects not followed, and no operator process reused or modified.

unresolved: The exact default 405 and page-not-found framing in a separately built production standalone runtime was not live-probed; the contract records the verified development-server behavior and source path.
Mixed-case tail route resolution on case-insensitive filesystems was not runtime-probed and remains platform-dependent.
A valid database-backed API-key last_used_at write was source-verified as possible but was not isolated in a live side-effect probe; its TTL/cache conditions are not universal requirements.
